notes.3: Task completion All bullet points must be answered in the correct tense/time frame and in the correct person, and appropriate opinions/reactions/explanations must be communicated where required by the task in order to gain full marks for Task completion. A mismatch between the subject and the verb will result in ambiguity and the message not being communicated clearly. Range Overall, candidates organised their work well, beginning each paragraph or new idea with an appropriate adverbial or prepositional phrase, but there was a lack of variety of sentence structures. Candidates who limit themselves to clauses introduced by parce que, car, qui, que are unlikely to progress beyond the 5–6 band. Some candidates were able to use more complex sentence patterns which gave them access to marks in the higher bands, e.g. mon grand père était content de me voir / elle m’a dit que les journées depuis sa retraite étaient incroyables / c’est difficile de rester en bonne santé quand on est âgé / quand je la vois sortir pour faire les courses elle fait des grimaces car elle a mal aux genoux / à mon avis, faire des activités dans mon quartier est un bon moyen de rester en contact avec tout le monde / ce que j’aime le plus dans mon quartier c’est qu’il y a beaucoup de magasins / je voudrais améliorer les transports en commun car ils polluent moins que les voitures. To access high marks for Range, candidates need to include a greater variety of linking words, e.g. relative pronouns and conjunctions, and use more complex structures. The use of object pronouns, infinitives after prepositions or modal verbs, comparisons and adverbs would enhance the complexity of their writing. Accuracy In both options, the general level of accuracy was modest. Control of basic grammar is essential for candidates to progress beyond the 3–4 band. The choice of the correct definite article, indefinite article or the appropriate partitive article was a problem for some candidates. The accuracy of spelling, gender, use of the appropriate article, placing and agreement of adjectives and elision are all critical, as is the correct choice of verb tense and form. Candidates need to spend time checking the accuracy of their essay. Verbs are critical to the effective passing of information. It is vital that candidates show their ability to manipulate verbs consistently in a variety of tenses and persons.
notes.3a: Une personne âgée dans ma famille For Task 1, candidates were able to give details about their elderly relative, e.g. je suis allé chez ma grand- mère qui a 80 ans / mon grand père habite au Brésil. A few candidates did not know âgée and some described a friend. �PAGE�31 0520 French June 2025 Candidates gave a range of different information to describe their visit in Task 2, e.g. j’ai pris l’avion pour aller voir mon grand-père / nous avons fait une promenade / j’ai aidé ma grand-mère à faire les courses. Candidates who understood Task 3 offered a range of information about how this person spends their time, e.g. il rencontre ses amis au café / elle joue aux cartes / il regarde la télévision. Candidates answered Task 4 with a range of difficulties faced by old people, e.g. les personnes âgées ont des problems de santé / elles sont seules à la maison / ils ont des difficultés avec la technologie. Task 5 was straightforward for candidates who could use a conditional tense correctly, e.g. je voudrais organiser une fête pour son anniversaire / je voudrais aller la voir avec toute la famille.
notes.3b: La vie dans mon quartier In answer to Task 1, candidates established the context of their visit with a simple statement, e.g. j’ai fait partie d’une association qui plante des arbres dans mon quartier / j’ai participé à un tournoi de foot. For Task 2, reactions to the experience ranged from the simple idea, e.g. j’ai adore cette activité, to the more compex, e.g. c’était une activité enrichissante / je pense que protéger notre planète est important. Some candidates only achieved partial completion of the task as they could not produce an appropriate past tense. For Task 3, candidates proposed a range of ideas, e.g. mon quartier est très tranquille / il n’y a pas de crime dans le quartier / les gens sont sympas. Some expanded their answer by mentioning disadvantages, e.g. il n’y a pas assez de poubelles, in anticipation of the following task. For Task 4, candidates also proposed a range of ideas, e.g. il y a trop de voitures / les gens jettent les déchets dans la rue / l’air est pollué à cause de la circulation et des embouteillages. Task 5 was straightforward for candidates who could use a conditional tense correctly, e.g. j’aimerais utiliser les transports en commun plus souvent / je voudrais acheter une voiture électrique / je voudrais planter des arbres et recycler le plastique.
notes.key_messages:
Candidates are advised to:
• give a single response, either single word or short phrase, for each gap in Question 1
• respond to all parts of Question 2 in the tense indicated
• use simple linking words in Question 2, for example when giving opinions/explanations
• choose the option in Question 3 which allows them to show what they know
• give brief additional details in response to individual tasks in Question 3
• plan and organise answers into a coherent piece of writing, using extended sentences where possible.
notes.general_comments:
Overall, candidates found the paper accessible, but common errors resulted in some candidates not able to
reach higher marks.
Candidates should be careful about the influence of words in their own language. Meaning was frequently
compromised when the following were replaced by a non-French word: agréable, autre, pays, pollution,
To convey their ideas, candidates must use a correct subject/verb accord in an appropriate tense.
It is important to copy correctly vocabulary given in the rubrics. The misspelling or incorrect gender of
améliorer, difficultés, personne, problèmes environnementaux, quartier sometimes compromised
communication.
Candidates are regularly asked to comment on advantages or disadvantages, and they should be able to
recognise such tasks and adapt the rubric used, e.g. l’avantage est / les avantages sont / l’inconvénient est /
les inconvénients sont.
Some candidates used trop/plus instead of très. These are not synonyms and can convey a different and
sometimes ambiguous meaning
Candidates should be able to write correct sentences and link them where possible using structures listed in
the syllabus, e.g. conjunctions (où, qui, que, quand, lorsque, si), verbal phrases (après avoir/être, avant de,
depuis, pour, afin de), correct prepositional linkage of verbs. Object pronouns, strong negatives and uses of
the comparative would also enhance the narrative.
